chunks.title: About Alfonso
chunks.text: Juan Alfonso Vega Sol (Alfonso) is a Computer Science student at the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering, focused on machine learning, deep learning and neural networks. He won 1st place at HackMX 6th Edition and Atrato Financial Hackathon, 1st Edition, and he founded Answr and ZapTap. He is based in the Seattle Area, WA.

chunks.title: What Alfonso is looking for and how to contact him
chunks.text: He's looking for a Summer 2027 internship in AI, ML or LLMs, and he's also open to software engineering roles. You can reach Alfonso at ponchovegasol@gmail.com or on LinkedIn. His email is ponchovegasol@gmail.com.

chunks.title: Founder & Software Engineer at Answr
chunks.text: Answr is an AI automation agency for local service businesses on Seattle's Eastside (Bellevue, Redmond, Sammamish, Kirkland). Alfonso's role: Founder & Software Engineer (Late 2025 — Present). He built an AI voice and SMS agent that answers missed calls, cutting first-response time from hours to under 30 seconds and recovering leads that were previously lost. He architected an event-driven automation stack on n8n, Supabase and the Claude API, orchestrating 20+ webhook-triggered workflows across lead capture, qualification, booking and follow-up. He engineered a structured-JSON prompting layer with input sanitization and a post-booking state lock, eliminating malformed responses and duplicate outreach. He designed and deployed the client-facing site and interactive demo in Next.js on Vercel, plus a two-tier plan architecture and a repeatable onboarding checklist. Stack: Claude API, n8n, Supabase, Next.js, Vercel, GoHighLevel and Airtable.

chunks.title: Founder at ZapTap
chunks.text: ZapTap is a business selling custom NFC review cards and tabletop displays that let local businesses collect Google reviews with one tap. Alfonso's role: Founder (Aug 2026 — Present). He built the full e-commerce site in Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4, deployed on Vercel. He implemented a React Context + localStorage cart with WhatsApp-based checkout. He designed a direct-response landing page where the section order is the persuasion sequence. Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React and Vercel.

chunks.title: Software & AI Team Member (AI/ML) at Fitness Tech
chunks.text: Fitness Tech is a student-led Engineering Student Organization at UW (40+ members, 6 projects) that builds wearable technology to streamline athletic training metrics. Faculty advisor: Prof. Sep Makhsous (ECE). Alfonso's role: Software & AI Team Member (AI/ML) (Oct 2026 — Present). He joined the Software & AI team on the AI/ML track. He is working across the full stack of MyFitnessTech, the club's Flutter app on iOS and Android that brings workouts, nutrition, sleep, hydration and biometrics into one profile with an AI coaching layer. Stack: Flutter.

chunks.title: Software Engineer at SAMLA
chunks.text: SAMLA is a financial web platform for inventory, profitability and payments. Alfonso's role: Software Engineer (Aug 2023 — Jan 2024). He built a financial platform with ASP.NET Core MVC and SQL Server: inventory tracking, profit analysis, break-even and ROI/ROCE dashboards. He integrated secure payments with Stripe and user authentication with role management. Stack: C#, ASP.NET Core MVC, SQL Server and Stripe.

chunks.title: IdentifEye
chunks.text: IdentifEye: Snap a photo of any product and get the closest match from Liverpool's catalog, plus LLM-powered recommendations. The problem: Liverpool asked teams to let customers find a product with nothing but a photo. Text search fails when you don't know what something is called, and the catalog was large and full of near-duplicate images. What Alfonso built: Image-embedding search on Vertex AI that matches any photo to catalog items. Recommendations for related products using GPT-4 Vision. Embedding-based duplicate removal for a catalog of any size. Concurrent microservices on Google Cloud, so one failure never takes down the web app. Live embedding storage in a database, optimized by 94% with concurrency and parallelism. React + Vite front end hosted on Firebase and Google Cloud Run. His role: Computer vision & AI. Team size: 5. Stack: Vertex AI, GPT-4 Vision, OpenCV, Flask, React, Vite, Google Cloud Run, Firebase and scikit-learn. Results: 1st place in the El Puerto de Liverpool AI Challenge at HackMX VI, out of 100+ competing teams. Liverpool publicly congratulated the team on LinkedIn. Award: 1st Place at HackMX 6th Edition (2025). Links: Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/identifeye. Year: 2025.

chunks.title: SkySAR
chunks.text: SkySAR: AI drone-swarm concept for search and rescue that flags people, vehicles and smoke in aerial imagery on a live dashboard. The problem: Search and rescue in forests and national parks is slow and sequential, and often happens in dense terrain without cellular coverage. What Alfonso built: An intelligence layer that uses Gemini Vision and computer-vision models to detect people, backpacks, vehicles and smoke in aerial imagery. A real-time, operator-friendly dashboard that prioritizes alerts for rescue coordination. A swarm design that searches large areas in parallel instead of sequentially. Ethics by design: data is collected only during active missions, with no continuous surveillance. His role: Developer & presenter. Team size: 6. Stack: Python, Gemini Vision, Computer vision and Web dashboard. Results: Community Impact Award at the ThinkCity 2026 Smart City Hackathon, representing Bellevue College. Award: Community Impact Award at ThinkCity 2026 (2026). Links: Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/skysar. Year: 2026.

chunks.title: Answr AI Agent
chunks.text: Answr AI Agent: Voice and SMS agent that texts back missed calls and books appointments, cutting first response from hours to under 30 seconds. The problem: Local service businesses like plumbers, HVAC companies, dentists and salons lose customers every time they miss a call. What Alfonso built: An AI voice/SMS agent with missed-call text-back, AI conversation and appointment booking. 20+ webhook-triggered automation workflows on n8n, Supabase and the Claude API, integrated with GoHighLevel and Airtable. A structured-JSON prompting layer with input sanitization and a post-booking state lock. Starter and Growth plan workflows, plus the client-facing site and interactive demo in Next.js. His role: Founder & software engineer. Stack: Claude API, n8n, Supabase, Next.js, Vercel, GoHighLevel and Airtable. Results: First response to missed calls went from hours to under 30 seconds. Eliminated malformed responses and duplicate outreach in the conversation pipeline. Links: Live site: https://answr.info; Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/answr. Year: 2025.

chunks.title: Can AI Spot a Lie?
chunks.text: Can AI Spot a Lie?: Fake-news classifier trained on 44,000+ labeled articles, with a dashboard of its metrics and the words behind each prediction. The problem: Misinformation spreads through emotional language, sensationalism and missing sources. Can a simple, explainable model catch those patterns? What Alfonso built: A text pipeline: cleaning, stopword removal and lemmatization with NLTK. TF-IDF features (unigrams + bigrams) and a Logistic Regression classifier trained on the Kaggle Fake and Real News dataset. A multi-page Streamlit dashboard with accuracy, precision, recall, F1, a confusion matrix and the most influential words per class. In-app model retraining from the sidebar. His role: Solo project. It was a solo project. Stack: Python, scikit-learn, NLTK, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn and Streamlit. Results: Presented at Making Learning Visible, Bellevue College's college-wide showcase (Dec 2025). Award: Presenter at Making Learning Visible (Dec 2025) (2025). Links: Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/can-ai-spot-a-lie. Year: 2025.

chunks.title: Ask Alfonso
chunks.text: Ask Alfonso: A small language model built from scratch (BPE tokenizer, decoder-only transformer and retrieval) that answers questions about his work. The problem: Recruiters have specific questions. A chatbot can answer them, but only if it never makes things up. What Alfonso built: A byte-pair-encoding tokenizer written from scratch. A decoder-only transformer: embeddings, causal multi-head self-attention, layer norm, MLP and residuals. TF-IDF retrieval that grounds every answer in this site's data, with a fallback when confidence is low. Guardrails that check every name, date and number in an answer against what the model read. A from-scratch TypeScript port that runs the whole pipeline in the visitor's browser. His role: Solo project. It was a solo project. Stack: Python, PyTorch, NumPy and TF-IDF. Links: Live demo: https://alfonsovegasol.com/ask; Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/ask-alfonso. Year: 2026.

chunks.title: FinanceAI
chunks.text: FinanceAI: AI assistant that answers questions about financial products and routes users to the right expert, with embedding-based cost optimization. The problem: Atrato wanted an AI virtual assistant that automates workflows by answering customer questions about its financial products. What Alfonso built: A question-answering assistant that also matches users to the right problem-solver from an uploaded employee database. Real-time API cost metrics, with costs reduced through embeddings and vectorized datasets. SQL-injection prevention on prompt input and hate-speech filtering on LLM output. A TruLens feedback loop to evaluate and improve answers. A responsive Streamlit app with light/dark mode, deployed on Streamlit Cloud. His role: Team member. Team size: 4. Stack: OpenAI API, LangChain, Hugging Face, TruLens and Streamlit. Results: 1st place at Atrato's Financial Hackathon, 1st Edition. Award: 1st Place at Atrato Financial Hackathon, 1st Edition (2024). Links: Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/financeai. Year: 2024.

chunks.title: Machine Learning Playground
chunks.text: Machine Learning Playground: Logistic regression from scratch, an MNIST neural network and a collaborative-filtering recommender in one interactive app. The problem: After Andrew Ng's Machine Learning Specialization, I wanted to prove I could implement the core ideas myself, not just pass the quizzes. What Alfonso built: Logistic regression from scratch in NumPy, predicting heart-disease risk on the Framingham Heart Study dataset. An MNIST digit classifier in TensorFlow/Keras with training progress and sample predictions. A recommender system using user and movie embeddings in a neural network (collaborative filtering). His role: Solo project. It was a solo project. Stack: Python, NumPy, Pandas, TensorFlow/Keras, scikit-learn, Matplotlib and Streamlit. Results: The MNIST classifier reached 97.33% test accuracy after 10 epochs. Links: Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/ml-playground. Year: 2025.

chunks.title: PDF Chatbot (RAG)
chunks.text: PDF Chatbot (RAG): Chat with any PDF: smart chunking, sentence embeddings, ChromaDB vector search and conversational memory. The problem: Long documents are hard to search. Retrieval-augmented generation lets you ask them questions instead. What Alfonso built: PDF text extraction and smart chunking. Hugging Face sentence embeddings stored in ChromaDB for vector search. Conversational memory and a Streamlit UI, with automatic CUDA/CPU handling in PyTorch. His role: Developer. Stack: Python, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face, ChromaDB, PyTorch and Streamlit. Links: Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/pdf-chatbot.

chunks.title: CSV Chatbot
chunks.text: CSV Chatbot: Upload a CSV and ask questions in plain English; a LangChain agent runs the Pandas queries. The problem: Not everyone can write Pandas code to explore a dataset. What Alfonso built: A LangChain agent powered by GPT-4 with full Pandas DataFrame manipulation. A Streamlit UI with one-command setup. His role: Developer. Stack: Python, LangChain, GPT-4, Pandas and Streamlit. Links: Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/csv-chatbot.

chunks.title: ZapTap
chunks.text: ZapTap: E-commerce site for NFC review cards, with a React Context cart and WhatsApp checkout. The problem: Local businesses need more Google reviews, and asking customers to search and type is too much friction. What Alfonso built: The full site in Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4. A React Context + localStorage cart and WhatsApp checkout with a pre-filled order message. A catalog in typed data files and a short, search-focused landing page for Google review cards. His role: Founder & developer. Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, React and Vercel. Links: Live site: https://zaptap.shop; Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/zaptap. Year: 2026.

chunks.title: SAMLA Financial Platform
chunks.text: SAMLA Financial Platform: Financial platform with inventory, break-even and ROI/ROCE analytics, Stripe payments and role-based auth. The problem: The business needed one place to track inventory, profitability and payments. What Alfonso built: Inventory tracking and profit analysis with break-even, ROI and ROCE metrics. Dynamic dashboards. Secure payments with Stripe and user authentication with role management. His role: Software engineer. Stack: C#, ASP.NET Core MVC, SQL Server and Stripe. Links: Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/samla. Year: 2023.

chunks.title: BlockCity
chunks.text: BlockCity: Unity game that teaches blockchain, AI and Web3, plus a companion site with an OpenAI-powered assistant. The problem: Blockchain, AI and Web3 concepts are hard to learn from text alone. What Alfonso built: A Unity (C#) game with thematic modules, quizzes, mini-games, rewards, cloud save and login. A companion website with a progress dashboard, profile management and an OpenAI-powered assistant. A serverless backend: Node.js on AWS Lambda + API Gateway, MySQL on AWS RDS, static hosting on S3. JWT auth with password encryption, CI/CD with GitHub Actions and unit tests with MSTest. His role: Developer. Team size: 5. Stack: Unity, C#, Node.js, AWS Lambda, API Gateway, MySQL, AWS RDS, S3, GitHub Actions and OpenAI API. Links: Demo video: https://youtu.be/BZy_tlWKUmU; Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/blockcity.

chunks.title: Ambient-Detectors
chunks.text: Ambient-Detectors: ESP32 device that streams temperature, humidity, CO₂, air quality and light into a live dashboard with alerts. The problem: Indoor air quality and comfort are invisible until something is already wrong. What Alfonso built: An ESP32-WROOM device with DHT11, MQ135, BH1750 and SCD30 sensors in a 3D-printed enclosure designed in Onshape. Arduino (C++) firmware sending readings over WiFi (HTTP POST) and I2C. A PHP API and MySQL database, plus a Streamlit dashboard with historical graphs and configurable alerts. His role: Developer. Team size: 2. Stack: ESP32, C++, PHP, MySQL, Python, Streamlit and Onshape. Links: Demo video: https://youtu.be/H2oz0zqGWlA; Case study: alfonsovegasol.com/projects/ambient-detectors.
